original_question: Let X be a projective hyperkahler manifold. If z in CH(X) is a Chow class that is a polynomial in divisor classes D1, ..., Dk from Pic(X) and in the Chern classes c_i(X), and if the cohomology class of z vanishes in H^*(X, Z), must z already vanish in the Chow ring?
target_in_paper: Conjecture 3 in Section 2.7 (Projective families): Beauville’s Chow-ring conjecture for projective hyperkähler manifolds.
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the substance of the paper’s statement almost verbatim: the ambient space is a projective hyperkähler manifold; one considers a class z in the Chow ring that is a polynomial in divisor classes coming from Pic(X) and in the Chern classes of X; the hypothesis is that the cycle class of z vanishes in cohomology; and the desired conclusion is that z itself vanishes in the Chow ring.
missing_details: The paper is in the complex-projective setting; here 'hyperkähler manifold' means Beauville’s irreducible holomorphic symplectic manifold, as defined earlier in Section 2.1.
The quantifiers are universal: for any finite collection D1,...,Dk in Pic(X), and any class z of the stated form.
The divisor classes D1,...,Dk should be understood as the corresponding classes in CH^1(X).
The notation c_i(X) should be made explicit as the Chern classes c_i(T_X) of the tangent bundle.
The cohomology group is the integral singular cohomology ring H^*(X, Z) of the underlying complex manifold, and the hypothesis is via the cycle class map CH(X) -> H^*(X, Z).
CH(X) is the total Chow ring with integral coefficients in the paper’s formulation, not a fixed codimension piece and not a rationally tensored Chow ring.
No homogeneity or fixed-codimension assumption is imposed on z; the paper allows any class in the total Chow ring obtained from such a polynomial expression.
No positivity condition (ample, nef, primitive, etc.) is imposed on the divisor classes D_i.
No nilpotency, asymptotic, or 'for sufficiently large m' condition appears anywhere in the statement.
refined_question: Let X be a projective hyperkähler manifold over C, in Beauville’s sense (equivalently, an irreducible holomorphic symplectic manifold). For any finite collection of line-bundle classes D1,...,Dk in Pic(X), viewed as divisor classes in CH^1(X), and any class z in the integral Chow ring CH(X) that can be written as a polynomial with integer coefficients in D1,...,Dk and in the Chern classes c_i(T_X), does the vanishing of its cycle class cl(z) in integral singular cohomology H^*(X, Z) imply that z = 0 in CH(X)?
justification: In arXiv:1002.4321, the exact paper-faithful target is Conjecture 3, stated in the section on projective families. Your draft is already extremely close to Beauville’s wording; the main refinements needed are only to make explicit the paper’s ambient complex-projective setting, Beauville’s meaning of 'hyperkähler', the interpretation of Pic(X) classes as divisor classes in CH^1(X), the fact that c_i(X) means c_i(T_X), and that the vanishing is tested by the cycle class map to integral singular cohomology. The paper does not add any degree, homogeneity, positivity, or asymptotic restriction, so a refined version should not introduce any.
